subject: Dedicated commit — packaging options, SLA trade-offs, and sizing proposal
messages:
From: Samuel Turner <sam.turner@fluxai.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring dedicated commit for production inference

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. FluxAI is evaluating a Dedicated GPU pool for our inference traffic — we need predictable throughput for our real-time feature extraction (low-latency scoring of user inputs). A few quick asks so I can prep for our internal finance/infra review: 

- Ballpark committed pool sizes you typically recommend for 20k active monthly concurrent users (we estimate ~400–600 QPS across peak shards).
- Typical throughput/SLA guarantees you provide (p99 latency targets, sustained TPS guarantees).
- How reserved commit discounts scale with term/size (12/24/36 months, and thresholds at 4/8/16 GPUs).

We ran a small load run with a community LLM (quantized 13B) and attached the CSV of the raw TPS trace and a zipped sample of traces. Can you take a look and advise on an initial commit and pricing range?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

— Sam
Head of Platform, FluxAI
[Attachment: fluxai-loadtest-summary-20270106.csv (CSV, 86KB)]
[Attachment: fluxai-traces-20270106.zip (ZIP, 4.1MB)]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Turner <sam.turner@fluxai.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Exploring dedicated commit for production inference

Sam — thanks for sending these. Quick read-through and some clarifying Qs before I pull pricing: 

1) Nice traces — a few questions about your test harness: what payload size (tokens) and model sequence lengths did you use for the runs? The per-request cost and GPU pacing will change with average token length.
2) Are you expecting stable sustained QPS per shard (e.g., 400 QPS sustained) or very spiky traffic with high tail bursts? We size Dedicated pools differently for spiky workloads (prefer smaller commit + burst) vs. steady throughput (bigger commit).
3) Any hard p99 latency SLO you must meet for product KPIs (e.g., p99 < 250ms)?

I'll loop in Marissa (pricing) and Karthik (capacity) to put together a short sizing + pricing playbook (we'll include committed pool options, canary fallback lanes, and recommended discount bands per term). If you can reply with the average token count and expected burst factor (1.5x, 2x), I'll draft a proposal by EOD Friday.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: canary-grafana-screenshot.png (PNG, 120KB)]

From: Samuel Turner <sam.turner@fluxai.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Exploring dedicated commit for production inference

Hi Laura — thanks for the quick reply. Details below: 

- Average prompt+generation size: 420 tokens (user prompt ~40–80 tokens, generation ~350 tokens).
- Traffic pattern: Mostly steady during business hours with two short peaks; overall we expect a burst factor of ~1.6x for 10–15 minute windows.
- Must-have latency: p99 < 300ms (hard requirement for product). 

I've included a short summary in the CSV header — highlights from the load run: sustained peak observed 520 QPS (50% of requests were light-cache hits), average p95 latency 180ms, p99 spikes to 420ms during KV cache misses. See attached traces for tail cases.

If it helps, we can also share a small sample of production traffic later this week.

— Sam
[Attachment: fluxai-loadtest-summary-20270106.csv (CSV, 86KB)]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samuel Turner <sam.turner@fluxai.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Exploring dedicated commit for production inference — fluxai load results

Forwarding FluxAI's load summary and traces. Key asks: sizing for ~520 QPS observed (1.6x bursts), avg 420 tokens/request, p99 requirement < 300ms. They ran quantized 13B in their harness — results show p99 tail at 420ms when cache misses occur.

Can you propose: 
- Two committed pool options (conservative and aggressive) with recommended GPU counts, expected sustained QPS, headroom for 1.6x bursts, and p99 latency forecasts.
- Pricing: committed monthly fee (USD) for 12/24/36 month terms and discount tiers for 4/8/16 GPU thresholds. Include a short note on optional burst credits and fallback to hosted at consumption rates for overflow.

Marissa/Karthik — please keep the note crisp; we'll send a summarized proposal back to Sam.

Thanks,
Laura

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exploring dedicated commit — sizing & pricing recommendation

LAURA / KARTHIK — see sizing/Pricing sketch below (attaching a simple workbook). Notes and assumptions up front:

Assumptions:
- Benchmark baseline: quantized 13B on our optimized runtime: ~85 inferences/sec per A100-80GB equiv for the reported avg request size (420 tokens) with KV cache behavior similar to their traces.
- Effective steady throughput per GPU (with caching, real workload): 65–75 infer/sec. Peak burst headroom w/ continuous batching: up to ~1.8x for short windows.

Sizing options (round numbers):
1) Conservative commit
- 8 x GPU pool (A100-eq)
- Estimated steady throughput: 520–600 inf/sec (meets their observed 520 QPS with modest headroom)
- Expected p99: ~220–280ms (with our KV cache configuration)
- Recommended burst credits: 50,000 GPU-seconds/month for short windows

2) Aggressive commit (lower unit pricing, more headroom)
- 12 x GPU pool
- Estimated steady throughput: 960–1080 inf/sec (ample headroom for 1.6x bursts)
- Expected p99: ~160–210ms
- Recommended burst credits: 120,000 GPU-seconds/month

Pricing (indicative, list USD/month):
- Per-GPU reserved baseline list: $18,000 / GPU / month (on-demand equivalent used for math).
- 12-mo term discounts: 8 GPU = 18% off list; 12 GPU = 22% off list.
- 24-mo term discounts: 8 GPU = 25% off; 12 GPU = 30% off.
- 36-mo term discounts: 8 GPU = 32% off; 12 GPU = 38% off.

Example math (12-mo):
- Conservative (8 GPUs): list $144k/month -> with 18% discount -> $118k/month. + burst credits at consumption rate ($2.50/GPU-second consumed beyond allotment).
- Aggressive (12 GPUs): list $216k/month -> with 22% discount -> $168.5k/month.

Other packaging notes:
- We can offer a performance SLO addendum for p99 latency with a small premium (approx +6% on committed price) that includes guaranteed prioritization, pre-warmed cache policies, and a dedicated ops oncall window.
- If FluxAI prefers flexibility, recommend 8-GPU commit + 4-GPU on-demand (burst) cushion; pricing would be blended (commit price on 8 GPUs + consumption pricing on 4).

I've attached a short workbook (sizing-estimate-20270108.xlsx) with the line-item math and a quick dashboard snapshot for the canary run. Let me know if you want me to tighten numbers for exec review.

— Marissa
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sizing-estimate-20270108.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)]

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Turner <sam.turner@fluxai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposal: 8 GPU committed pool (12-mo) with optional SLO addendum — next steps

Sam — thanks for the data and patience. Attached is a concise proposal summary; below is the short version to move to procurement: 

Proposal highlights:
- Recommended starting commit: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent), 12-month term. This meets observed 520 QPS with ~10–15% steady headroom and supports their 1.6x short bursts with configured burst credits.
- Monthly committed price (12-mo): $118,080 (8 GPUs at list $18k -> $144k less 18% discount).
- Optional SLO addendum: +6% on committed price to guarantee p99 < 300ms with prioritization and pre-warm policies. If FluxAI needs the SLO, we recommend taking it given their product requirement.
- Burst strategy: 50k GPU-seconds/month included; overflow billed at a discounted consumption rate. We can also structure a blended option (8 GPU commit + 4 GPU reserved burst) if they want more deterministic pricing for overflow.

Next steps: 
1) Confirm term length (12/24/36 mo) and whether SLO addendum is required.
2) If yes, we'll issue a draft contract and DocuSign proposal (link below).
3) Upon signature, we schedule a canary rollout with a 48-hour soak and joint ops runbook.

Proposal doc: https://www.docusign.com/FLX-2027-001/proposal
Grafana snapshot for canary: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/fluxai/canary-ops?orgId=1

Would you like a short call Monday to walk execs through the tradeoffs?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
